Every other generic atom/red gets isspacep.local/.global branches (:670-724). A predicated generic atomic, or an op other than add/and/or/xor/exch/cas, throws (:593-594, :627-629). The 1531 descriptors are built from map_basic_info (extra_buffer becomes base, max_thread_count becomes shards: nv_attach_impl.cpp:1022-1030). Nothing in the pass checks other uses of a 1531 result: plain loads, stores or 32-bit atomics through it are not refused. DESIGN.md:85 ("not admitted") has no code behind it today.

Any type the chain does not name falls through to host_call (:342, :436, :462), which is the one-slot CommSharedMem protocol (:140-180; gpu_helper_protocol.h:22-84). Plain hash maps and 1501 go that way today: 1501 has a constant at :72 but no branch. For 1531, the lookup is pure address arithmetic in sum_array_offset (:266-277): NULL without a device copy or with fewer than 32 shards, and the shard is ((smid & (shards/32-1))<<5)|laneid with shards in max_thread_count. Update returns -1 (:370-372) and delete returns -1 (:458-461). So today no trampoline map path reads or writes map memory with ordering. The trampoline PTX has no .relaxed/.acquire/.release, no nanosleep, no red., and only 32-bit atom.*.b32 (grep of trampoline_ptx.h). Its atomics come from 32-bit generic __nvvm builtins (:17-29), and its fences are membar (:109-116). map_info is built per attach by bpf_attach_ctx::create_map_basic_info (runtime/src/attach/bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:509-571, called at bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:642-643). It takes extra_buffer from bpf_map_handler::get_gpu_map_extra_buffer (map_handler.cpp:1878-1937), whose first call allocates and zeroes the 1531 device copy (nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:722-770). It takes max_thread_count (the shards for 1531) from map_handler.cpp:1866-1871. It is written into each patched library by write_trampoline_globals (nv_attach_impl.cpp:2491-2508, via cuLibraryGetGlobal and write_library_global :2464-2487) and, on the late path, by nv_attach_fatbin_record.cpp:312-341. trampoline_ptx.h is checked into git. The default CLANG is clang++-17, which is not installed; clang++-16 is. Every compile rewrites the module's .target to the device's arch (rewrite_ptx_target nv_attach_utils.cpp:31-67, called from compile_ptxs nv_attach_fatbin_record.cpp:147-175, which throws when the arch is unknown, and from wrap_ptx_with_trampoline_for_sm :69-73). touch_points.for_1533: Add a branch that accepts only (flags & 0xffffffff) == BPF_NOEXIST. BPF_ANY, BPF_EXIST and BPF_F_LOCK go to an error, and DESIGN says -EINVAL. The insert follows the decided order. Walk as lookup does. At an empty slot, `atom.relaxed.gpu.global.cas.b64` the slot from 0 to {K, claiming}. The winner does a single `atom.acq_rel.gpu.global.add.u64` on the count, and the old value is the row. If row >= max_entries, it publishes a permanent {K, refused} with `st.release.gpu.global.b64`, counts the refusal and returns -E2BIG. Otherwise it does `red.global.add.u64` of *(u64*)value into its own shard of that row, then publishes {K, row, live} with `st.release.gpu`. There is no give-back and no second counter. A live K returns -EEXIST, counted. A CAS lost to K means a bounded wait (nanosleep loop) for live, then -EEXIST; on timeout, -EEXIST plus an unstable count. A CAS lost to another key continues the walk. A new constant is needed for -EEXIST (-17), and for -EINVAL (-22) if used. The 5th argument stays unused. No copy means an error return, not host_call (:436).

risks: The walk can hang the kernel. DESIGN.md:29's termination argument (at most max_entries claimed, so half the slots stay empty) no longer holds under the decided CAS-first order, because refused headers keep their slots. Distinct keys arriving after capacity can fill all slots, and the per-thread-key tools DESIGN expects to get E2BIG are exactly that load. An uncapped walk in _bpf_helper_ext_0001/0002 would then spin forever in the application's kernel. Both walks need a cap of `slots` steps: lookup returns NULL, insert returns -E2BIG and is counted.

Refused-header semantics are not decided anywhere. Neither the task nor DESIGN says what a lookup of a refused K returns, what an insert of K returns when it finds K refused, or what a loser waiting on K does when the header becomes refused instead of live. The trampoline needs all three answers.

Loss counters can become a hot spot. On first touch with a constant key, every thread but one gets EEXIST. Counting that on one device word is the 'hot key without shards' case in DESIGN's cost table, 1.09-1.10 ns per thread measured. Counters may need (SM, lane) shards the way sum_array_offset spreads 1531's adds (default_trampoline.cu:266-277); warp collectives are excluded by the design.

Layout copies can disagree. The header encoding, hash and block offsets will exist in trampoline C++, in the agent's prefill (host), and in PTX text if the inline path is built. A mismatch gives silent misses or a second slot for one key. Put them in gpu_helper_protocol.h with static_asserts and test that the copies agree.

A missing device copy must not fall through. Without one (another process owns the map, as nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:703-720 rules), the 1533 branches must return NULL or an error, as 1531 and 1532 do (default_trampoline.cu:268-270, 297-298). Reaching host_call at :342/:436/:462 would update the CPU hash table, which is not the truth after the copy.

New PTX forms: nothing in today's trampoline PTX uses .relaxed/.acquire/.release, nanosleep, red., or 64-bit atom. They are accepted only because the target is rewritten to sm_87 before ptxas. Check C3 has to confirm the SASS on the real llama.cpp modules, including the register and occupancy effect of a noinline helper that now contains a loop.

Return codes change convention. The trampoline returns -1 and -7 today. -EEXIST (-17) and -EINVAL (-22) would be new constants for GPU programs, while host-call updates return resp.map_update.result (default_trampoline.cu:447).

risks: The CAS-first change breaks DESIGN.md:29: 'at most max_entries are ever claimed, so at least half stay empty'. A winner refused at capacity keeps its slot for good, so each distinct refused key consumes a slot. Per-thread-key tools (DESIGN.md:42) fill the directory. GPU walks, CPU lookups, CPU get_next_key and the agent's seeding inserts must all be bounded by the slot count and treat 'no empty slot' as E2BIG.

Rows are the count's old values. A refused winner's add still advances the count, so after refusals count > max_entries. The seeding step must set count = number of seeded keys, and delivery and the CPU must ignore rows >= max_entries.

No 1531 pattern exists for a CPU-writable phase followed by a seal: 1531 refuses updates always (nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:114-120). A loader update racing the agent's key snapshot can be lost unless the seal excludes in-flight writers. The hash's stripe locks are the only existing exclusion. A process killed holding one hangs, as CLAUDE.md 'Hash Map Concurrency' documents.

OWNER_PID takeover (nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:705-721): a second process after the owner's death gets a fresh zeroed block. For 1531 that only resets counts. For 1533 it also drops every key unless the new owner re-seeds from the delivered directory.

The copy is made for every map at the first CUDA link (bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:642-643 -> bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:523-531). A loader that prefills after the target's agent instantiated its links gets EPERM. Prefill must precede the agent's start, as pt_loader.c:64-99 does before attach.

The delivery is not an atomic snapshot across words (1531 the same, nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:420-428). A CPU reader may see a live header whose row sum is from an older delivery. Header-before-row ordering needs the acquire fence, which today's snapshot PTX lacks.

Companion naming: map names are truncated to 15 bytes in attr->map_name, so a suffix rule can collide. Neither a runtime-created companion nor MAP_GET_NEXT_ID enumeration is reachable by tools (syscall_context.cpp:1246-1248).
1531 delete returns EINVAL, not EPERM (nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:122-126), contrary to DESIGN.md:96. Pick one for 1533 and fix the doc.

Delivery: a directory with live, claiming and refused headers plus sharded and single rows. CPU lookup and get_next_key return only live keys in slot order; walks stop at the slot bound with a full directory (mutation: refused treated as empty -> duplicate slot; unbounded walk -> hang).
Owner takeover: a second process after the owner's exit keeps the keys (re-seeded) or documents their loss.

risks: The CPU probe walk can miss keys the slot-by-slot snapshot delivers. Snapshot threads read slots independently (cpp:168-193), so a key of a kernel that no covered sync waited for can be delivered live at slot j while a slot between its home and j, read earlier, is delivered empty. lookup then misses a key that get_next_key returns. Keys of covered kernels are always reachable: their walk's slots were claimed before the kernel completed, so the sync chain at cpp:350-357 makes those claims visible to the snapshot. So SYNCS_COVERED keeps its meaning for covered keys only. Options, none chosen: CPU lookup scans all S_slots; a host-side fix after the copy marks such slots occupied until the next delivery; the snapshot rereads a live key's predecessors after its acquire. In every case claiming and refused slots must be delivered as occupied, never as empty.

Header-before-value order: 1531's copy loop (cpp:420-428) writes words in ascending index order with relaxed stores, and readers order only on DELIVERIES (cpp:101). With an interleaved [header][value] mirror, a reader sees a newly live key with value 0 or an older value. Values must be stored first, then a release, then headers, with an acquire on the header read.

The decided change (CAS first; a refused winner keeps its slot permanently) means claimed slots are bounded by the distinct keys ever tried, not by max_entries. DESIGN.md:29 ('at least half stay empty, every probe sequence ends') may no longer hold. The snapshot iterates slots and stays bounded, but device walks, CPU lookup and get_next_key each need a step cap of S_slots. Flag for the design owner.

Readers memcpy after elem_lookup returns (syscall_context.cpp:969), concurrently with the next delivery's relaxed stores. Formally that is a C++ data race; per word it is the same as 1531 today and acceptable for u64 sums. Multi-word or store values would need the synthesis's seqlock, which belongs to the undecided store layout (DESIGN.md:111-119), not to stage one.
One shared s.broken and one module: a set-up or snapshot failure of the hash entry stops 1531/1532 delivery for the whole process (cpp:334-339, 414-419).

tests: None exist today for delivery (no test references deliver_now, SYNCS_COVERED or BPFTIME_GPU_DELIVERY_*). New ones below.

Snapshot kernel (GPU; skip without one): a hand-built device block with headers empty, claiming, refused, live row < R and live row >= R, and known shard values. Staging must hold the raw headers and the exact sums for live slots only. Mutations: summing non-live rows; claiming delivered as empty; reading R-row shards as single copies.

Mirror ordering (CPU only): a writer thread copies synthetic staging into the mirror, turning keys live with nonzero values, while reader threads look them up. A key read as live must never carry a value lower than the one staged with it. Mutation: headers pass before values pass (or interleaved ascending) gives value 0.

Lookup vs get_next_key consistency: synthetic staging with slot i empty and slot i+1 live for a key whose home is i. Pin down the chosen behaviour, and check that every key get_next_key returns is found by lookup when that is the rule.

Covered syncs end to end (GPU): a kernel inserts N keys with BPF_NOEXIST and adds; then cudaDeviceSynchronize, then deliver_now(false). Every key must be live with the exact sum minus the counted EEXIST, with SYNCS_COVERED == app_sync_count. Repeat with BPFTIME_GPU_DELIVERY_AT_SYNC=1.

Prefill: CPU updates before the device copy are present after get_gpu_mem_buffer, each in shard 0 of rows 0..k-1, with count = k. A CPU update after the copy returns EPERM. Race: a tool updates while the agent copies; no update may be lost without EPERM.
Owner rule: a second process gets no device copy (NULL), as with 1531.
Lifetime: the tool closes the map fd while the delivery runs, with no use-after-free. Mutation: 1533 left out of the pin list at map_handler.cpp:1921-1941.
Refused-slot fill: distinct keys past max_entries fill the table with refused headers. CPU lookup and get_next_key must end (step cap) and report E2BIG counts through the companion status array.
Failure isolation (if separated): a forced failure of the hash entry leaves 1531 delivery running.

Map types are recognized in one place on the attach side: nv_attach_impl::route_thread_local_maps_of_module (attach/nv_attach_impl/nv_attach_impl.cpp:1007-1067). It walks map_basic_info and builds a sum_map_desc for each 1531 map {fd, base=extra_buffer, value_size, max_entries, shards=max_thread_count} (1022-1030) and a thread_local_map_desc for each 1530 map (1032-1040). A 1532 map only sets a flag so that the pass runs (1013-1021). With none of the three present it returns the PTX unchanged (1042-1043). hack_fatbin calls it once per PTX file, after every kernel's pass and only if some kernel was modified (1222-1226); it then prepends the trampoline (1227-1228). The direct-run path calls it too (1349-1358). The per-kernel pass cache is keyed on the request JSON, which holds no map data (1118-1215). Patched images are cached per fatbin (2394-2426).

Today 1531's device address reaches a patched module in two ways, and neither is a per-map global:
- **Baked into the PTX:** the routing pass writes it as an immediate into each constant-fd lookup it inlines (nv_thread_local_routing.cpp:759-802 sum_lookup, gated by sum_has_copy 733-737, called from route_function_body 1163-1189).
- **Read at run time:** the trampoline reads map_info[fd].extra_buffer (default_trampoline.cu:266-294). map_info is a `__constant__ MapBasicInfo[1024]` (40960 bytes, trampoline_ptx.h:18). It is written whole with cuLibraryGetGlobal + cuMemcpyHtoD after the patched image loads (nv_attach_impl.cpp:2466-2510, called at 2582), together with constData and __bpftime_pid_tgid. The late path does the same with cuModuleGetGlobal (nv_attach_fatbin_record.cpp:311-345).

The device copy itself is made at attach time, inside the agent, by create_map_basic_info (runtime/src/attach/bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:642-643, then bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:509-571). That calls map_handler.cpp:1921-1941, then nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:683-775: owner-PID CAS, shards = next_pow2(SMs) x 32, cuMemAlloc, zeroing on its own stream, then register_device_array for delivery. It happens once per process.

Adds through a lookup result that only sum lookups define become cvta.to.global + atom/red .global (nv_thread_local_routing.cpp:1259-1267, 654-669); other atomics get an isspacep-guarded generic form.
